summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of GeTe films with tunable Te composition using trichlorogermane (HGeCl3) and bis(trimethylsilyl)telluride [(Me3Si)2Te] as precursors at low temperature (60 °C). The process involves the use of a unique ALD of elemental tellurium (Te) using tellurium ethoxide [Te(OEt)4] and (Me3Si)2Te as precursors, allowing for the formation of GeTe x films with controllable Te content. The films exhibit uniform and conformal morphology on high aspect ratio structures, and the study highlights the importance of controlling the Te:Ge atomic ratio for the development of ovonic threshold switching selectors and phase change memories.
evidence: The growth of GeTe resulted in moderately Ge rich films independently of the ALD precursor injection time and the use of single or discrete (Me3Si)2Te doses. To achieve control over the GeTe film composition, the authors developed a unique ALD of elemental tellurium (Te) using tellurium ethoxide [Te(OEt)4] and (Me3Si)2Te as precursors. Combining GeTe and elemental Te in an ALD supercycle fashion, they obtained GeTe x films with a controllable Te content showing a uniform and conformal morphology on high aspect ratio trench structures.
